description: Introduces wetland ecosystems with emphasis on principles and problems associated with their functions and values as related to water quality. Become familiar with basic and applied concepts in hydrology, soils, and vegetation of both constructed and natural wetlands.

name: Water Resource Sustainability
description: Quantitative effects of human impacts on hydrologic ecosystems (aquifers, watersheds, coastal zones, lakes, and wetlands). Case studies illustrate detrimental effects of unsustainable resource utilization and beneficial management strategies.

name: Soil Microbial Ecology
description: Occurrence and activities of soil microorganisms and their influence on soil productivity and environmental quality.

name: Ecology of Waterborne Pathogens
description: Survival strategies, gene regulation and metabolism of waterborne pathogens. Methods for microbe detection and control.

name: Soil and Water Chemistry
description: Physico-chemical processes such as mineral weathering and formation, sorption, and ion exchange. Also includes introduction to diffuse double-layer theory.

name: Aquatic Toxicology: Science and Applications
description: Introduces foundational knowledge and concepts of the field of aquatic toxicology. Examines how environmental and chemical properties influence the fate and bioavailability of contaminants in aquatic environments; introduces principles of toxicology and methods used to study aquatic toxicology, as well as applications of knowledge gained from aquatic toxicology studies.

name: Soils, Water and Public Health
description: Important instances where soil and water science and public health overlap; develop skills required for competency in both disciplines.

name: Soil Physics
description: Physical processes and properties of soils that influence optimum growth of plants as well as potential for groundwater pollution from agrochemicals and applied wastes. Primary emphasis is given to basic concepts of transport and retention for water and solutes; secondary emphasis is given to air and heat in the root zone of the soil profile; and limited attention is given to mechanical properties of soil that affect the proliferation of plant roots.

name: Environmental Pedology
description: Study and analysis of soil in the environment and the factors responsible for soil formation and geographic distribution. Development of hydric soil criteria and hydric soil indicators. Emphasis on morphology or hydric/ non-hydric soils and introduction to diagnostic horizons and soil classification. Course also includes abs on soil field techniques.

name: GIS in Soil and Water Science
description: Basic, practical understanding of GIS concepts, technical issues, and applications to soil and water science using ArcGIS geographic information system.

name: Environmental Soil and Water Monitoring Techniques
description: Introduces the principles, objectives, and practices in environmental monitoring. Learn the proper techniques in planning for monitoring projects, sampling design, sample collection, basic principles of laboratory analysis, and basic data analysis. Also introduces and emphasizes quality assurance and quality control requirements.

name: Supervised Extension Experience in Soil and Water Sciences: SUPERVISED EXTENSION EXP
description: Firsthand, authentic extension experiences in agricultural and life sciences under the supervision of a faculty member. Projects may involve program planning, development, implementation, and evaluation.

name: Individual Work
description: Selected topics for qualified students.

name: Supervised Research in Soil and Water Science: SUPERVISED RESEARCH IN SWS
description: Provides firsthand, supervised research. Projects may involve inquiry, design, investigation, scholarship, discovery, or application.

name: Honors Thesis Research in Soil and Water Science: HONORS THESIS RESRCH IN SWS
description: Independent research in soil and water science leading to an honors thesis. Student will be mentored by a faculty member. Projects may involve inquiry, design, investigation, scholarship, discovery or application.

name: Special Topics in Soil and Water Science: WETLANDS SEMINAR
description: Variable topics designed to meet students' needs and interests.

name: Full-time Practical Work Experience in Soil and Water Science
description: Practical work must be a new experience and related to field of study.

name: Soils for Environmental Professionals
description: Fundamentals of soil properties and processes that explain the central role soils play in the environment. Geared to environmental professionals with little knowledge of soil science. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Environmental Nutrient Management
description: Consumption, manufacture, properties, and reserves of fertilizer materials. Methods of application, effects on soil reaction, and plant requirements of fertilizer nutrients. Understanding specific fertilizer reactions. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Tropical Soil Management
description: Characteristics and management of tropical soils. Technologies that minimize industrial inputs.

name: Earth System Analysis
description: Analysis of global-scale interdependences between climate, biogeochemical cycles and humans using a systems approach.

name: Sustainable Agricultural and Urban Land Management
description: Studying agricultural and urban water quality issues in Florida, their bases, land and nutrient management strategies, and the science and policy behind Best Management Practices (BMPs). Students will learn to evaluate BMP research and analyze its role in determining practices and policies that protect water quality.

name: Environmental Biogeochemistry
description: Overviewing of the biogeochemical processes affecting elemental cycling (carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, sulfur) in global environmental systems.

name: Environmental Soil, Water, and Land Use
description: Suitability of soils for different uses. Proper use of soil survey reports, topographic maps, and related information. Relationships between land uses and water behavior in soils and landscapes. Water use and allocation. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Water Resource Sustainability
description: Quantitative description of human impacts on hydrologic ecosystems (aquifers, watersheds, coastal zones, lakes, and wetlands). Case studies show the detrimental effects of unsustainable resource use and beneficial management strategies. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Hydric Soils
description: Concepts, field identification, and delineation of hydric soils. Instruction in accordance with the National Technical Committee for Hydric Soils and with regulatory agencies. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Wetlands and Water Quality
description: Introduction to natural and constructed wetland ecosystems. Problems associated with eutrophication and water quality. Hydrology, soils, and biogeochemistry. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Soil Microbial Ecology
description: Occurrence and activities of soil microorganisms and their influence on soil productivity and environmental quality. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Ecology of Waterborne Pathogens
description: Modern methods for molecular and cultivation-dependent identification of soil- and waterborne pathogens. Risk assessment. Survival strategies, gene regulation, and metabolism of waterborne pathogens outside of their mammalian hosts. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Soil and Water Chemistry
description: Theoretical background and current approaches to agricultural and environmental problems. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Soil Chemical Analysis
description: Practical and theoretical aspects of instrumentation and techniques commonly used in analyzing soils and plants.

name: Soils, Water, and Public Health
description: Highlights important instances where soil and water science and public health overlap. Develops skills required for competency in both disciplines.

name: Environmental Soil Physics
description: Transport processes for water, solutes, gases, and heat in the root zone. Important soil properties (physical, chemical, and biological) that influence the transfer processes characterized in the field and laboratory. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Environmental Pedology
description: Soils in the environment. Heavily oriented toward field applications of pediogical principles and processes. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: GIS in Land Resource Management
description: Introduction to basic concepts and use of "Arc GIS" to address land resource management issues. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Environmental Soil and Water Monitoring Techniques
description: Introducing students to the principles, objectives, and practices in environmental monitoring. Students will learn the proper techniques in planning for monitoring projects, sampling design, sample collection, basic principles of laboratory analysis, and basic data analysis. Quality assurance and quality control requirements are introduced and emphasized.

name: Fertilizer Technology and Use
description: Presents the basic concepts of fertilizer technology as tools for effective agricultural crop nutrient management. Provides information on a wide range of fertilizer technologies and application methods from nationally and internationally known researchers and industry experts. Detailed understanding of how to produce different fertilizer components and how to use them properly to improve plant use efficiency.

name: Soil Quality
description: State-of-the-art studies/knowledge on soil quality. Principle assessment of soil quality with respect to biological production, plant and animal health, food security, and environmental quality. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Soil and Nutrient Diagnostics for Agricultural Production
description: Field nutrient management using basic soil fertility concepts with scientific diagnostic techniques in various soils and cropping systems will be discussed. Nutrient budgeting for effective agricultural best management practices for agricultural and environmental sustainability will be included.

name: Urban Soil and Water Systems
description: Issues and opportunities related to soil and water quality in urban systems. Students will learn and discuss consequences of human population growth on soil and water systems in urban areas.

name: Advanced Microbial Ecology
description: Phylogeny and evolution; diversity of habitat; genetic exchange.

name: Biodegradation and Bioremediation
description: Principles of biodegradation of toxic organic chemical; practices in conducting biodegradation studies in soils and water, and in microbial aspects of bioremediation of contaminated soils and water.

name: Soil Health and Data
description: Examine the concept, history, and underlying science of soil health; Apply basic statistical methods to analyze soil data and assess soil health in the R programming environment; Compare and select soil health indicators; Discuss the management practices for enhancing soil health.

name: Biogeochemistry of Wetlands and Aquatic Systems
description: Biogeochemical cycles of carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, sulfur, and redox cations in wetland soils and sediments, as related to their agronomic, ecological, and environmental significance. Also offered as distance education course.

name: Advanced Biogeochemistry
description: Global elemental cycles in terrestrial, wetland, and aquatic systems as related to water quality, carbon sequestration, and climate change.

name: AI Modeling in Soil and Ecosystem Sciences
description: AI Modeling to Understand the Properties and Functions of Soils and Ecosystems.

name: Modeling Soil, Water, and Ecosystem Processes
description: An introduction into predictive modeling of soil, water, and ecosystem processes. Students learn from the ground up how to transform a conceptual model into a mathematical framework that then will be coded up in a simulation model. This hands-on experience serves the students to recognize how data can best serve models and how models can be used to interpret real world data.

name: Modeling Land Biogeochemistry
description: Modeling the flow of water, carbon and nutrients from an Earth system perspective.

name: Special Problems
description: Laboratory, library, and/or field study and research in a particular aspect of soils. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Supervised Research
description: Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Journal Colloquium in Environmental Science
description: A discussion-based course to help graduate students in environmental science fields develop skills for critical analysis of literature while exploring current literature topics.

name: Seminar
description: Presentation of literature, methods of proposed thesis research, and selected topics.

name: Topics in Soils: WETLANDS SEMINAR
description: Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Supervised Teaching
description: Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Professional Development in Soil, Water, and Ecosystem Sciences
description: This course serves as a professional development component to graduate coursework in soil and water sciences and related fields. Topics include common skills and challenges in academia and professional employment. This course is available to both MS and PhD students and is offered every fall and spring semester.

name: Research for Master's Thesis
description: Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Aquatic Toxicology: Science and Applications
description: Introduces foundational knowledge and concepts of the field of aquatic toxicology. Examines how environmental and chemical properties influence the fate and bioavailability of contaminants in aquatic environments; introduces principles of toxicology and methods used to study aquatic toxicology, as well as applications of knowledge gained from aquatic toxicology studies.

name: Advanced Research
description: Research for doctoral students before admission to candidacy. Designed for students with a master's degree in the field of study or for students who have been accepted for a doctoral program. Not appropriate for students who have been admitted to candidacy. Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Research for Doctoral Dissertation
description: Also offered as a distance education course.

name: Readings in Swahili
description: Readings in Swahili

name: Development of Sociological Thought
description: Comparative study of the principal contributors to the development of sociology. Emphasizes relevance of these ideas to contemporary social thought and current social issues.

name: Methods of Social Research
description: Introduces the scientific method and its application to social science research. Includes research design, data collection and computer data analysis and interpretation.

name: Writing in Sociology
description: Helps sociology majors improve the quality of writing professional sociological reports.

name: Individual Work
description: Examines topics/areas/issues not covered in regularly scheduled courses.

name: Undergraduate Research in Sociology: UG RES SOCIOLOGY
description: Provides firsthand, supervised research. Projects may involve inquiry, design, investigation, scholarship, discovery, or application.

name: Special Study: INTRO TO CONSERVATION CRIM
description: Various specialized topics/areas/issues not covered in regularly scheduled courses.

name: Department Honors in Sociology: Dept Honors Sociology
description: Department honors course.

name: Internship in Sociology: INTERNSHIP
description: Supervised experience in a sociology-related organization or agency. Emphasizes the application of academic knowledge to real-world situations while developing career-relevant skills. Course assignments complement internship experiences by guiding students in setting individualized goals, identifying areas for growth, and reflecting on vocational pathways.

name: Classical Social Theories
description: Sociological theory from its inception in the early 19th century to about 1930. The ideas of Comte, Spencer, Marx, Weber, Simmel, Durkheim, Pareto, Mead, and others.

name: Contemporary Sociological Theory
description: The study of modern sociological theories, roughly 1930 to the present.

name: Qualitative Research Methods
description: Fieldwork, observation, participant observation, and other qualitative data-collection and analysis techniques.

name: Research Design in Sociology
description: Covers major social science research designs and techniques for conducting empirical inquiry into social phenomena. Emphasis on practical skills, epistemological approaches, and critical evaluation of research designs and methods, with a focus on developing a research agenda or a proposal for the dissertation, thesis, or research grant.

name: Quantitative Research Methods
description: Applying selected quantitative methods to sociological research problems. Extensive practice applying the methods.

name: Professional Development in Sociology
description: Introduction to professional practices in sociology and criminology. Overview of research ethics, science communication, and other elements of professional practice in research and teaching. Review of scholarly literature in one’s research topic as a first step toward a research proposal. Required for sociology and criminology graduate students.

name: Individual Work
description: Work on subjects not available in currently offered courses.

name: Supervised Research
description: Supervised Research

name: Applied Social Research Project: Appl Social Res Proj
description: Supervised individual or team applied research project.

name: Research for Master's Thesis
description: Research for Master's Thesis

name: Sociological Application of Network Science
description: Discussion of social networks as patterned structures of relationships among individuals and/or groups. Focus on social network analysis, which provides tools to understand why and how macro-level social forces beyond the individual operate through social interactions at a more micro level. Learn theories and techniques to systematically understand interpersonal and/or intergroup dynamics that make a societal-level change possible.

name: Advanced Quantitative Methods in Sociology
description: Review of regression models with random or fixed effects. Introduction to the latest advanced quantitative methods such as resampling methods, machine learning-based regression models, and econometrics methods for causal inference. Application of quantitative methods to empirical studies.

name: Special Study in Sociology: Wisdom, Individual and Society
description: Special Study in Sociology

name: Advanced Research
description: Research for doctoral students before admission to candidacy. Designed for students with a master's degree in the field of study or for students who have been accepted for a doctoral program. Not appropriate for students who have been admitted to candidacy.

name: Research for Doctoral Dissertation
description: Research for Doctoral Dissertation

name: Transnational Sociology
description: Examines comparative and transnational approaches by emphasizing a cross-border research perspective in studying social transformation occurring across the globe within trans-local and transcontinental contexts. Explores transnational migration, identity and belonging, transnational religion, global cultural diffusion, transnational business, transnational crime, and social movements.

name: Sociology of Globalization
description: Examination of diverse forms of worldwide interconnection, including economic ties, political ties, and ecological ties. A study of how global interdependencies and inequalities link the fates of people around the planet and how “Globalization” is a form of political discourse that shapes policy-making and alters how lives are lived globally.

name: Urban Sociology
description: The development of cities and their spatial and social structure. Critical problems and solutions. Integration of people in the social setting. Social implications of city planning. (S and N)

name: Sociology of Race and Racism in the US
description: Sociological analysis of the structure, social processes, and efforts to construct race and racial inequality in the US.

name: Gender and Health
description: Examines gender differences and similarities in health and illness in the United States. Uses a broad focus on health and illness across the life course and integrates social and biomedical determinants of health.

name: Population
description: Characteristics and trends in the populations of the contemporary world. Historical and current growth patterns related to resource conservation, food production, and modernization in various regions of the world.

name: US Population Issues
description: Introduces major issues related to US population size, growth, and composition. Covers historical and contemporary population issues and introduces basic demographic measures and sources of data.

name: Environmental Sociology
description: Survey of sociological ideas concerning environment-society interactions, environmental changes, and social responses. Evaluation of sociological theories regarding environment-society topics, problems and conflicts. Examination of case studies about environment society interactions from the US and other countries.

name: People, Places, and Belonging
description: An interdisciplinary and discussion-oriented course on the complex and dynamic ways place fundamentally shapes our personal and public lives. Wide-ranging examples to show how place-related circumstances affect efforts to promote personal empowerment, civic engagement, and social and environmental justice. Exploration of social processes related to place-based claims, attachments, rituals, and transitions.

name: Sociology of South Asia
description: Examines social change and development in South Asian societies, contextualizing their distinct histories and global relevance, including ties to the U.S. Topics encompass contested histories, identity politics, nationalism, democratization, growth, poverty, and inequality. Features diverse case studies from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.

name: Nationalism and Ethnicity in Europe
description: Comparative study of the roles played by nationalism and ethnic identity in modern Europe.

name: Sociology of Gender
description: Examines the social construction of gender in everyday life; how gender structures social institutions such as the economy and mass media; and how gender shapes the distribution of resources, power, and privilege in ways that benefit men over women.

name: Reproduction and Gender
description: Examines contemporary reproductive issues in the US. How culture and social structures shape the reproductive realm and how the social psychology of individuals' influence their reproductive experiences.

name: Men and Masculinities
description: Focuses on issues related to traditional and emerging images of masculinity in the past, present and future. Emphasizes relationships between social forces and males' everyday life experiences across the life-span. (S and D)

name: Core Issues in Environmental and Resource Sociology
description: Addressing the origins and current status of Environmental and Resource Sociology (ERS), central theoretical debates among ER sociologists, and focal topics of concern to ER sociologists, with emphasis on ERS topics current among ER sociologists at the University of Florida.

name: Environmental Governance
description: A social scientific examination of governance policies, rules, and practices that shape environmental outcomes and regulate human-environment relations.

name: Sociology of Race and Racism in the U.S.
description: Overview of racial-ethnic oppression, stratification, and conflict in the U.S.

name: Introduction to Sociology
description: In this course, students will gain an understanding of the basic sociological concepts and vocabulary, including the methodological tools, sociological perspectives, and scientific procedures used by social scientists to collect data and conduct research. Topics generally include: society and culture, institutions, socialization, influences, crime, change, groups, sex, race and ethnicity, family, class and population.

name: Social Problems
description: The development, analysis, and treatment of social problems. Crime, poverty, prejudice and discrimination, pollution and environmental despoliation, and drug abuse and mental illness. Emphasizes factors in US society that cause social problems.

name: Global Social Problems
description: Treatment of social problems such as inequalities in a global context. Consideration of perspectives from multiple social science disciplines to examine globalization and social problems as well as global policy frameworks to address those problems. Hands-on virtual exchange experience to explore cross-cultural dimensions of social problems.

name: Marriage and Family
description: Introduction to concepts, theories, and research methods in the sociology of marriage and family. Review of historical and current trends, including family structures, romantic relationships, cohabitation, marriage, childbearing, parenthood, gender, sexuality, aging, work-family issues, and inter-generational care giving. Analysis of patterns, causes, and consequences related to individual choices, social interactions, institutional influences, and policies regarding relationships and families.

name: Overseas Studies: Euro Cultures&Identities
description: Provides a mechanism by which coursework taken as part of an approved study abroad program can be recorded on the UF transcript and counted toward graduation.

name: Poverty
description: The social, cultural, economic, political and psychological implications of being poor. Sources of poverty in the structure and operation of society and the consequences of poverty for society. Current and feasible policies for easing the problem in the contemporary United States with reference to its past and to other nations, both developed and underdeveloped.

name: American Families
description: The impact of rapid social changes upon families, including race, class and ethnic variations. The liberation of women and changing family roles. Alternative life styles and the futures of families.

name: Political Sociology
description: Applies sociological analysis to political themes in a comparative context.

name: Medical Sociology
description: Effects of group characteristics in the causation, amelioration and prevention of mental and physical illness and social influences in medical education, medical practice and hospital administration.

name: Social Inequality
description: The unequal distribution among individuals and groups of wealth, power and prestige; the effect of class systems upon society; the effect of class membership on individuals; social mobility.

name: Digital Inequalities
description: Uses a sociological perspective to examine inequalities in access, use, and impact of digital technologies on people in the United States. Includes attention to workforce development and training in the digital economy. Compares positive, negative, and neutral impacts of digital technologies across social strata.

name: Society and the Individual
description: Relation of the individual to the social environment with special reference to person perception, self-formation, self-disclosure, attitude formation and change, and group structure and processes. Social forces that shape the lives of individuals and how individuals adjust to modern society. (S)

name: Deviance
description: Introduces the sociology of deviance: the definition of deviance; types of deviant behavior such as suicide, drugs, and alcohol abuse, sexual deviance, deviant subcultures and violence; differential labeling and institutional processing; and implications of social control.

name: Sociology of Human Sexuality
description: Theoretical and conceptual issues, empirical research, and social policies germane to human sexuality in the US. Topics include sexual identity and orientation, sexual behavior, social control of sexuality, social implications of STDs and HIV/AIDS, and the relationship between sexuality and the sociopolitical process.

name: Empathy, Leadership, and Civic Engagement
description: Examines the processes that frame how we manage the relationship between the “me” and “we” in our culture. Showcases how skill-building initiatives to promote MEAL life skills (mindfulness, empathy, altruism, and leadership) can empower people while producing healthier social systems. It also illustrates strategies to create supportive environments to promote personal growth, community engagement, and social justice.

name: Criminology
description: Nature and causes of crime, criminality and criminal careers. Research in crime and delinquency. Sociological analysis of criminal law, criminal justice, rehabilitation, punishment, prevention and deterrence.

name: Sociology of Aging and Life Course
description: Social and personal conditions of post-retirement years; family and housing patterns; income, leisure, health, and group processes; evaluating institutional care for the aged.

name: Sociology of Aging and the Life Course
description: Social and personal conditions of post-retirement years. Family and housing patterns, income, leisure, health, group processes, and evaluation of institutional care of the aged.

name: Introduction to Federal Income Tax
description: Introduces federal income taxation to those who pursue careers in accounting; develops a basic understanding of the federal income tax laws relating to businesses and provides a framework for integrating income tax planning into the business decision-making process.

name: Federal Income Tax 1
description: First of a two-course sequence studying the concepts found in the Federal income tax code. Primary emphasis will be using the income tax code to understand gross income, income exclusions, as well as deductions for businesses.

name: Federal Income Tax 2
description: Second of a two-course sequence studying the concepts found in the Federal income tax code. Primary emphasis will be using the income tax code to understand property transactions in a business and investment context.

name: Tax Professional Research
description: Use of professional tax literature and technology for problem solving. Case-based to provide experience in dealing with unstructured situations encountered in professional tax practice. Emphasizes problem identification and resolution.

name: Corporate Taxation
description: In-depth study of taxation of corporate formations and ongoing operations. In addition, this course provides an introduction to accounting for income taxes.

name: Advanced Corporate Taxation
description: Second of a two-course sequence that continues the study of corporate taxation. The course emphasizes: liquidations, reorganizations, divisions; it introduces the taxation of S corporations.

name: Partnership Taxation
description: Providing depth of knowledge in partnership taxation. Required for students pursuing the "tax" track. Elective for other MAcc. students.

name: International Taxation
description: Expansion of introduction to international tax, addressing more complex concepts encountered by U.S. multinationals operating abroad. U.S. taxation of foreign persons with U.S. activities included.

name: State and Local Taxation
description: Tax issues involved when business enterprises operate in multiple taxing jurisdictions. Principles of both multi-state and international income taxation (and their overlap).

name: Acting for Change
description: Explore art's potential beyond entertainment in this course. Examine performance theories, diverse genres, and works across media to uncover how theatrical techniques can drive social change. Engage with theorists’ writings, study various performances, and workshop methods to harness creative energy for meaningful impact.

name: Autobiographical Literature & Performance
description: Explores how modern and contemporary American artists and writers utilize self-examination as the basis for artistic creation. Often merging the factual with the theatrical or dramatic, autobiographical performance and literature personalizes the values, incidents and relationships that shape human experience and give life meaning.

name: Theatre Appreciation
description: In this course, students will explore dramatic structure, techniques, and various organizational elements. The course provides an introduction to theatre as a collaborative art form through the critical analysis of its historical context, production, theory, and connections to theatrical literature, including the Western canon.

name: American Musical Theatre History
description: This course approaches American Musical Theatre through lenses of identity and representation reflecting current discourse around the art form. Participants will investigate the ways in which culture and community have been represented on stage through music, choreography, acting, directing, and design over a century of performance. Special attention will be paid to the ways in which American Musical Theatre has reiterated, resisted or transformed harmful stereotypes.

name: African American Theatre History and Practice
description: Examines origins and development of theatre by, for, and about Black Americans

name: Diversity and Multiculturalism in American Theatre
description: Development of images of marginalized peoples as presented in the American Theatre from Colonial period to the present.

name: History of Theatre on Stage 1
description: Surveys the history of dramatic literature and stage performance from Greek and Roman times to the Restoration, including Japan and India. Concentrating on plays, theatrical spaces and performance practices of each era in the context of social and artistic movements. (N)

name: History of Theatre on Stage 2
description: Continues the survey of THE 4110 from the 18th century to the present, with featured segments on African and contemporary world theatre. Particular emphasis on the 19th century and the emergence of modernist movements: realism, expressionism, Artaud, Brecht. (N)

name: Latin American and US Latinx Theatre
description: Theatre created by Latin American and US Latinx playwrights and performers has served as a vehicle for both artistic expression and social and political change. Organized geographically, this course considers themes and trends in Latin American and US Latinx Theatre in light of issues such as hybridized identities, language, immigration, oppression and generational conflict. Representative works by Latin American and US Latinx playwrights will be examined.

name: History of Musical Theatre 1
description: Historical elements and the development of music theatre from Gilbert and Sullivan through 20th century styles. Historical information is directly applied to the literature of music written for operettas, oratorios, minstrel shows, vaudeville, burlesque, musical reviews, dance theatre, and musical comedies. Shows and composers that promoted change in musical theatre development are also studied.

name: History of Musical Theatre 2
description: Historical elements and the development of music theatre from Gilbert and Sullivan through 20th century styles. Historical information is directly applied to the literature of music written for operettas, oratorios, minstrel shows, vaudeville, burlesque, musical reviews, dance theatre, and musical comedies. Shows and composers that promoted change in musical theatre development are also studied.

name: Cognizant Design Theory
description: Focusing on the intersection of historical, social, and cultural awareness and theatrical design, students will investigate critical social movements in design while examining the impact design choice has on the individual and society. Cognizant Design Theory challenges conventional thinking regarding the nature of design and creativity, empowering meaningful representations of cultures and peoples in theatrical design practice.

name: Production Dramaturgy
description: Introduces the field and concepts of production dramaturgy. Includes script analysis, text editing, research, adaptation, new play development, season selection and programs. Students complete a production protocol.

name: Individual Study
description: A reading, research or performance project.

name: Special Topics in Theatre: Israeli Arab Conf-Stage&Screen
description: Lecture, seminar or studio sessions covering selected topics of current interest in theatre.

name: Summer Repertory Theatre
description: Practical experience in repertory theatre with direct skills application in all areas of theatre production.

name: Production Workshop: Scene
description: Participation in the production program of the curriculum with work in preparation and performance. Focus on area of specialization.

name: Senior Project
description: Final project presented in public performance demonstrating expertise in declared area of specialization.

name: Senior Project
description: Senior project for Bachelor of Arts theatre majors. Completion of a research project and/or preparation of a dramaturgical project to be undertaken with advisor's consent in the final semester.

name: History, Literature, and Criticism I
description: Readings and discussions of Western and Japanese dramatic literature and criticism from their beginnings to the 18th century.

name: History, Literature, and Criticism II
description: Discussions of dramatic literature, performance theory, and stage practice from the 19th century to the modern and postmodern of Western, Indian, Chinese, and African cultures.

name: Seminar in Creative Process: Solo Work (MFA)
description: Specialists in all areas of theatre explore the similarities in their creative thinking and methods.

name: Individual Study: Stagecraft
description: Reading, research, or performance project.

name: Special Topics: Cognizant Design Theory
description: A graduate level lecture, seminar or studio sessions covering selected topics of current interest in theatre/theatre studies.

name: Arts and Public Health Professional Seminar
description: The online course provides a practical orientation to professional competencies, practice, and ethics for the arts and public health. The professional seminar will focus on core issues, trends, and critical debates central to current practice, and historical and contemporary applications of the arts in the field of public health.

name: Supervised Teaching
description: Supervised Teaching

name: Internship
description: Practical experience in residence with a professional theatre or equivalent.

name: Applied Theatre: Costume
description: Specialized practical experience achieved through participation in realized productions.

name: Summer Repertory Theatre
description: Practical experience in repertory theatre, directly applying skills in all areas of theatre production.

name: Project in Lieu of Thesis
description: Creative project in lieu of traditional written thesis.

name: Introduction to Live Entertainment Design and Production
description: Creating live performance onstage, backstage, and offstage defines the collaborative art of the School of Theatre and Dance (SoTD). This course serves as an introduction to the environment of production within the school while broadening the student’s understanding of the larger ecosystem of the industry. Cirque du Soleil to the Hippodrome Theatre live performance is defined by the engagement of the collective; this course breaks down, explains, and promotes understanding across all areas.

name: Drawing and Rendering
description: Drawing and painting techniques unique to the theatre. Emphasis on portfolio development and media experimentation: watercolor, markers, charcoal and acrylics.

name: Scene Painting
description: Utilization of advanced and experimental techniques unique to theatre graphics; exploration of various media for 3-dimensional representation in scene and design and model building.

name: Beginning Makeup
description: Introduces the skill and artistry of theatrical makeup.

name: Stagecraft
description: Introduces skills and craft of technical theatre. Includes knowledge of materials, techniques, tools, and supplies basic to the execution of environment; requires additional laboratory hours.

name: Beginning Costume
description: Introduces skills and craft of costume design and execution. Knowledge of materials, techniques, and tools basic to revelation of character.

name: Drawing/Drafting for the Stage
description: Techniques and basic principles of drafting as applied to stage design: lights and sets.

name: Practical Stage Lighting
description: Fundamentals of stage lighting for live events, CAD schematic drawing, lighting fixtures, digital controls and technical methods and practices.

name: Costume Technology I
description: Focuses on intermediate level pattern drafting, fitting, alteration, and construction techniques for costumes. Rotating topics include Tailoring I and Draping I.

name: Introduction to Sound Design and Technology
description: This course introduces the students to the basics in sound design and technology. Students will work on projects about design elements and design process. Students will also work in the electric shop and/or productions assignments.

name: Arts Administration
description: Introduces the practical skills required for the successful management of arts organizations. Areas covered include community and civic engagement in the arts, budgeting, marketing, fundraising, audience development, contracts, board governance, and issues associated with the founding of a nonprofit organization.

name: Lighting Design
description: Lighting aesthetics, design, and control; application of principles of design to lighting in the theatre.

name: Lighting Design 2
description: Advanced lighting design with focus on automation programming and presentation techniques.

name: Costume Design
description: Application of fundamentals of costume design to various genres of dramatic literature.

name: Scene Design
description: Studies the basic processes and functions of scenic design within theatrical production. Development of the ability to create spaces based on scripts and choreography.

name: Advanced Theatre Graphics
description: Specialized study in scene painting with focus on professional studio work and union examination.

name: Digital Design for Theatre and Dance 1
description: Unlock a diverse spectrum of artistic possibilities using technology to support choreography and live performance and nurture new technical and artistic sensibilities for manipulating time, space, shape, and motion. (Only offered at New World School of the Arts in Miami).

name: Advanced Crafts for the Stage
description: Emphasizes advanced materials construction for the designer/technician in scenic design and technical direction.

name: Costume Technology II
description: Focuses on advanced level pattern drafting, fitting, alteration, and construction techniques for costumes. Rotating topics include Tailoring II and Draping II.

name: Sound Design
description: Guides students through the exploration of the functions of sound and music, the evolutionary origin of theater, and how a sound designer/composer can take advantage of this knowledge in their work. This course closely follows the textbook. Details of the projects can be found in the textbook.

name: Sound Design 2
description: This course introduces the students to the operations in different aspects of audio production. Students will learn to use a digital audio workstation (Digital Performer 9) through lectures, exercises and projects.

name: Advanced Sound Design
description: In depth investigation of one rotating topic: Audio Drama, Music Composition for Theatre, Audio for Video, Music Production, or Musical Theatre Mixing. Additional topics are possible based on need and interest.

name: Commercial Theatre Industry
description: Provides an overview of the theatre as an industry in America today. Major topics include Broadway, Off Broadway, project development from both creative and business management aspects, touring, and other types of theatre ventures.

name: Theatrical Producing
description: An examination of commercial theatrical producing, focusing on current developments and trends on Broadway, Off-Broadway and in Broadway touring. Analysis of case studies featuring guest speakers from leadership positions in Broadway management, production, and artistic roles. Participation in a field study of a national touring production.

name: Producing for Regional Theatre
description: Examines nonprofit regional theater in the United States by focusing on marketing, creative marketing strategies, maximizing earned revenues through dynamic subscription ticket sales, advertising and public relations, grant writing, and successful fundraising from individual, corporate, foundation, and government sources.

name: Stage Management
description: Introduces the principles and techniques of stage management, explores practical application, and examines topics specific to the work of a stage manager.

name: Special Topics in Theatre Production: Entertainment Desgn Fundamntls
description: Lecture, seminar, or studio sessions covering selected topics of current interest in theatre production.

name: Advanced Stage Management Seminar
description: This seminar serves as a forum for peer sharing and problem solving on current production assignments. Rotating topics are specific to the stage management profession and industry trends.

name: Lighting Specialties: Rotating Topic
description: This course investigates, in depth, one of the following rotating topics. Façade lighting, dance lighting, lighting control/programming, basic architectural lighting, museum and gallery lighting, themed entertainment lighting, retail and interior lighting, light and health, advanced lighting design rendering. Additional topics are possible based on the need and interests of the students.

name: Internship in Theatre Design or Production
description: Work with a professional theatre, dance, ballet, opera company, or other approved professional situation.

name: Production Practicum
description: Production experience in the design or execution of department productions.

name: Lighting Design I
description: Advanced applications. In-depth practice of design concept formulation, use of advanced equipment, and complex scenographic documentation. Introduction to CAD for the lighting designer.

name: Lighting Specialties
description: This course investigates, in depth, one of the following rotating topics. Façade lighting, dance lighting, lighting control/programming, basic architectural lighting, museum and gallery lighting, themed entertainment lighting, retail and interior lighting, light and health, advanced lighting design rendering. Additional topics are possible based on the need and interests of the students.

name: Costume Design I
description: Emphasizes character and play analysis for the costume designer.

name: Scene Design I
description: Study and practice of the scenic design process. Developing scenic design techniques for theatre and dance. Emphasizes script analysis for the scenic designer.

name: Graduate Scene Painting
description: Advanced techniques in scene painting. Developing textural illusion, and enhancing volume through light and shadow.

name: Advanced Theatre Graphics
description: Rendering for theatrical design. Traditional techniques, computer aided applications, and model building.

name: Costume Technologies Workshop: Costume Crafts
description: Costume crafts work through realized projects. Possible topics: millinery, stage jewelry, masks, prosthetics, wigs, puppetry, footwear, and dyeing.

name: Design Studio
description: Investigation of design theory, research, concept, and presentation used in production of theatre and dance.

name: Lighting Design II
description: In-depth study of processes. Refinement of aesthetic concept, complex productions, state-of-the-art technologies, CAD applications, and lighting for built environment.

name: Costume Design II
description: Advanced study. Specialized costume design problems for individual projects.

name: Detail Design for Costume Designers
description: Intensive study and practical application of designing specific motifs and accessories for costumes.

name: Scene Design II
description: Design work in a variety of genres. Complex multi-set productions.

name: Costume Construction
description: Detailed study of patterning and construction techniques used in men's and women's dress. Extensive hands-on work with contemporary and historical garments.

name: Pattern Making: Draping
description: Advanced study of draping methods of costume creation. Extensive hands-on work using the sculptural qualities of fabric and clothing.

name: Computer Drafting 2D
description: Study of computer aided drafting for the theatrical designer. Emphasizes techniques for the scenic and lighting designer.

name: Special Topics: Professional Development
description: A graduate level lecture, seminar or studio sessions covering selected topics of current interest in theatre design and/or production.

name: Acting for Non-Majors
description: The discipline and the creative process of acting, including formal and improvisational techniques for developing vocal, physical and analytical skills applicable to a variety of theatre styles, including those from the Western canon. (H)

name: Acting 1: Instrument and Discipline
description: Introduces the craft of acting through basic physical, vocal and analytical concepts, methods, vocabulary, and discipline. Also explores the creative process through exercises in observation and awareness.

name: Professional Development Seminar 1: BFA Theatre Performance majors
description: Lab to be taken concurrently with Acting I, and serves as a forum for discussion, master classes, and guest lectures from faculty, staff, and industry professionals. Develop skills to address the emotional, physical, and psychological demands of being a professional actor.

name: Musical Theatre Auditions and Business Management
description: Focuses on developing the student’s ability to connect and combine managerial, economic and business-related skills necessary for a career in Musical Theatre in the 21st century. The course covers information regarding auditions/auditioning, agents/managers, unions, marketing strategies, publicity, networking, finances, time management.

name: Musical Theatre Workshop
description: Preparation and performance in song and dance ensemble in musical revues and cabaret; development of style, interpretation and flexibility.

name: Acting for the Camera
description: Principles and techniques of various performance methods in acting for television and motion pictures.

name: Movement Training for the Actor 1
description: Emphasizes physical preparation and character development through movement. Focusing on the preparation of the body, this course aids the actor's approach to performance.

name: Somatics for the Actor I
description: Introduction to psychophysical processes that offers actors an alternative way of thinking about character embodiment beginning with basic physical awareness and the exploration of self. Somatics, from the Greek word for the living body, soma, is the study of the body experienced from within. Conditioning the evolving actor as an artist is a mind/body exercise: strength, balance, flexibility, alignment, and imagery come together as a balanced whole.

name: Acting 2: Analysis and Application: BFA
description: Experimentation with scripted material: scene study, analysis, audition and performance.

name: Professional Development Lab 2
description: Serves as a forum for performance laboratory, discussion, master classes, and guest lectures from faculty, staff, and industry professionals. To be taken concurrently with Acting 2.

name: Acting 3
description: Emphasizes versatility and expanding the repertory of roles through physical, vocal and psychological transformation.

name: Beginning Improvisation
description: The fundamentals of improvisation; learn performance techniques concerning conceptual agreement, character creation, team building, and active listening in order to create intelligent and honest scenework.

name: Acting 3/2
description: Continuation of the third level acting course with emphasis on beginning the development of the professional actor's knowledge of theatre repertoire.

name: Voice and Movement 3/2
description: Offered in Miami only.

name: Fundamentals of Music Theatre Acting
description: Acting techniques, character research, and audition strategies as applied to musical theatre material.

name: 20th Century Musical Theatre
description: Analysis and preparation of roles from music theatre genres of the 20th century. Exploration of vocal styles and staging.

name: 21st Century Musical Theatre
description: Analysis and performance of the 21st century musical theatre canon by examining styles, repertoire and context. Also examines vocal skills, choreography techniques, and audition techniques.

name: Acting for Dance
description: Offered in Miami only.

name: Movement Training for the Actor 2
description: Character development through movement analyses; exploration of the physical demands pf performance; practical applications of movement vocabulary to aid the actor's search for believability.

name: Directing
description: Practical application of theoretical concepts of directing applied to scene study.

name: Devising Theatre
description: Introduction to devised theatre, which is the process of theatre creation in a collaborative manner. Explores the collaborative process of original work created by a group of artists who in many instances are also the performers. Exposes a variety of processes in ensemble theatre-making, including adaptation, group-writing, found text, improvisation, working with counterpoint, and creating solo performance, as well as methods of offering criticism.

name: Somatic Acting for the Actor II
description: A continuation of Somatics for the Actor I with an emphasis on an application of somatic studies as applied to character work. Topics may include methods such as Feldenkrais Movement Through Awareness, The Lucid Body, the Franklin Method, Mindful Movement Exercises, or others.

name: Script Analysis
description: Formalist approach to teach the skills of script analysis for actors, directors, and designers.

name: Acting 4
description: Continuation of Acting series, TPP 3103 / 3113 / 4114.

name: Advanced Improvisation
description: A seminar in performing continuous improvised pieces; students learn to recognize, play, and heighten the "game of the scene" in a number of long-form structures.

name: Acting 5: Shakespeare
description: Experimentation and experience with classical literature: analysis and performance.

name: Acting Style: 18th Century to Post Modernism
description: Experimentation and experience with the stylistic techniques, analysis, and performance of plays from the 18th century to Post-Modernism.

name: Strategies for the Career Actor
description: For those with serious intent on pursuing professional careers in the field. Explores the primary facets of the business of being an actor in the context of a major entertainment market including (but not limited to) relevant philosophical aspects, marketing and promotion, professional representation, auditioning and the development of an effective practical skill set to procure and secure employment and sustain a lifelong career in the industry.

name: BFA Actor Senior Workshop
description: Capstone course for all BFA Acting students. Student actors study, experiment and produce in laboratory.

name: Voice for the Actor
description: Recover and free the voice and integrate the body, mind, and emotions of the actor in finding clear and honest expression in performance.

name: Speech for the Actor
description: Continuation of TPP 4287, emphasizing speech training for the actor. Study speech anatomy and physiology and move to a very full overview of phonetics based on a linguistic model and apply this knowledge to acting.

name: Comedy Practice
description: Learn to find your comic voice through the creation and performance of late night joke writing, standup, and sketch comedy.

name: Stage Combat: Unarmed and Light Weaponry
description: Introduces stage combat techniques including unarmed, rapier and dagger and/or single sword. Emphasizes safety and control.

name: Playwriting Workshop
description: An introductory workshop in playwriting, culminating in the creation of a complete, one-act play by each student.

name: Actors Workshop
description: Basic stage dialects with emphasis on standard British, Irish, American-Southern, American-New York and French. (Using International Phonetic Alphabet.) Offered in Miami only.

name: Actors Workshop 2
description: Offered in Miami only.

name: Special Topics in Theatre Performance: Vocal Extremes & Voice Overs
description: Lecture, seminar or studio sessions covering selected topics of current interest in theatre performance.

name: Professional Development Seminar
description: Lab serves as a forum for discussion, master classes, and guest lectures from faculty, staff, and industry professionals. Topics supplement material in acting technique courses.

name: Internship in Theatre Performance
description: Work with a professional theatre or other approved professional situation.

name: Musical Theatre Practicum
description: Production experience in the execution of department productions. Participation in the production program of the curriculum with work in preparation and performance of a roles or roles. This course meets regularly during scheduled class sessions and requires attendance at all scheduled rehearsals and performances for the musical.

name: Repertory Company
description: Offered in Miami only.

name: Graduate Acting I: Modern Acting Theory and Practice
description: Diagnostics of analytical and technical skills of acting through exploration of psychological realism through the use of psycho-physical exercises.

name: Graduate Acting II: Shakespeare and High Style
description: Analytical, research and technical skills needed to perform plays written in "high verse" with particular focus on the plays of Shakespeare. Students will be directed in the formalist approach to classical performance style. The approach is designed to enhance each student's awareness, development, and capability for heightened performance requirements.

name: Graduate Acting III: Period Styles
description: The stylistic techniques, analysis, and performance of plays from ancient Greek to the early twentieth-century. The course is designed to enhance the imaginative artistry of the student and to develop awareness and capabilities for heightened performance techniques.

name: Acting IV: Contemporary Realism: Realism 2
description: Investigating the fundamental principles of acting technique. Over a series of progressive exercises, students continue to discover an effective, dependable, repeatable set of working tools for the actor, derived from the teachings of contemporary acting theorists, to enhance their sense of purposefulness, immediacy and truthfulness in their performance work.

name: MFA Company Acting Workshop
description: Stdent actors study, experiment, and produce in a laboratory emphasizing specialized skills and methods; and nonrealistic and period genres.

name: Acting for the Camera
description: Investigating acting technique relative to the specific constraints and demands of the film/television medium. In addition, the class helps to prepare the actor to procure work in the industry through discussions of and explorations focused on the business aspects of being a professional actor.

name: Voice and Movement I
description: Vocal skills, emphasizing versatility, production, power, and strength.

name: MFA Voice and Speech II: Shakespeare and High Styles
description: Vocal skills unique to the execution of nontraditional and period roles. Continued development of a virtuoso vocal instrument through exploration and experimentation with consonant, structural, and tonal energy. A coherent approach to voice, speech, text, and actor preparation. Emphasis on Verse Drama and Heightened Style.

name: The Alexander Technique I: Somatics
description: Introducing fundamental principles of the Alexander Technique (AT); a mind-body approach to the use of self as applied to acting.

name: The Alexander Technique II
description: Investigating the fundamental principles of the Alexander Technique (AT) introduced in Alexander Technique I. The course includes basic anatomy, developmental movement, breathing and relaxation techniques, and presentations.

name: Directing
description: Explores the philosophy and psychology of directing and the director. Applied to scene study.

name: Graduate Movement Training: Techniques for the Actor (MFA)
description: Helping the actor move freely and explore characterization through movement. This course introduces students to Period Styles and Social Deportment in order to develop awareness and capabilities for heightened performance techn

name: Graduate Stage Combat
description: Instruction in standard stage combat techniques of Unarmed and Rapier & Dagger. Safety is emphasized in the creation of the illusion of armed and unarmed violence.

name: MFA Voice and Speech III: Period Styles
description: Emphasizing specialized voice an speech skills and methods of specific to the style of dramatic literature from ancient Greek to the early twentieth-century.

name: MFA Voice and Speech IV: Advanced Vocal Training for the Actor
description: Graduate Voice and Speech course emphasizing specialized skills and methods specific to modern and contemporary plays, film and television, and voice-over.

name: Special Topics: Stories for Sustainability
description: A graduate level lecture, seminar or studio sessions covering selected topics of current interest in theatre performance.

name: ESOL and Reading for Teachers
description: Develop an understanding of literacy teaching and learning, with a dual focus on native speakers of English and English language learners; focuses on methods and materials used to support the development of proficient and critical adolescent readers in academic content areas.

name: Introduction to Teaching English as a Second Language
description: Historical overview of trends in language teaching technology, ranging from communicative approaches to techniques for teaching listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Preparation for instructing small groups and individuals in English language skills.

name: Pronunciation for Teaching English as a Second Language
description: Overview of sound system of North American English and its integration with listening, morphology and spelling. Pronunciation pedagogy based on current theory and practice, as well as diagnostic tools and assessment measures.

name: ESOL Foundations: Language and Culture in Classrooms
description: Examines issues of language and culture relevant to school-age learners of English as a Second Language (ESOL).

name: ESOL Curriculum, Methods and Assessment
description: Examines factors that affect second-language learners’ participation and learning in elementary classrooms. Emphasizes designing curriculum, materials, and assessments that promote effective instruction for both native English speakers and second-language learners.

name: ESOL Strategies for Content Area Teachers
description: Overview of the issues relevant to English as a Second Language (ESOL) learners and develops the skills to teach ESOL students in content area classes.

name: Teaching English as a Second Language Internship
description: Capstone course available only to undergraduates in TESL certificate program. In cooperation with the English Language Institute, teaching interns observe classes, shadow teachers, review materials and, in teams, create and implement special noncredit short-term courses for English language learners.

name: ESOL Curriculum, Methods, and Assessment
description: Curriculum, methods, and assessment for second language learners in K-12 classrooms.

name: ESOL and Reading for Secondary Teachers
description: This course is designed to develop students’ understanding of literacy teaching and learning, with a dual focus on native speakers of English and English Language Learners. It focuses on methods and materials that can be used to support the development of proficient and critical adolescent readers in academic content areas.

name: Curriculum and Materials Development for ESOL K-12
description: Developing and adapting standards-based curriculum and materials for L2 oral language and literacy, academic content, and K-12 ESOL instruction.

name: Language Principles for ESOL Teachers
description: Applied linguistics for teachers. Language-acquisition theories related to learning a second language in school. Connections between language and literacy development and effective instruction for English language learners.

name: Methods of Teaching ESOL K-12
description: Effective oral language and literacy instruction for K-12 English language learners.

name: Technology for Language and Reading Education
description: Explores foundational issues at the intersection of technology and language and reading education. Prepares students to research, create, and evaluate technologically enhanced instruction and assessment for foreign language education (FLE), English for speakers of other languages (ESOL), and reading education in K-20 contexts.

name: Testing and Evaluation of ESOL
description: Introduction to assessment issues and experience in developing assessment techniques for learners of English as a second language.

name: Issues in ESOL for School Counselors and Psychologists
description: Gives school counselors and psychologists an overview of key concepts and issues related to ESOL students in K-12 schools.

name: Transportation Engineering
description: Overview of the significance of highway transportation to the social and economic underpinnings of society. Introduces road vehicle performance, geometric design of highways, traffic flow and queuing theory, highway capacity and level of service analysis, traffic control and analysis at signalized intersections, and travel demand and traffic forecasting.

name: Urban Transportation Planning
description: Overview of the four-step urban transportation planning process; includes analytical techniques for estimating future travel demand and state-of-the-art approaches.

name: Traffic Engineering
description: General review of the fundamentals of traffic engineering with emphasis on field studies and data analysis.

name: Transportation Systems Analysis
description: Systems analysis in transportation planning and engineering, including supply, demand, equilibrium, evaluation and decision analysis.

name: Transportation Facility Design
description: Simulates a comprehensive design of a transportation facility, specifically an arterial-freeway interchange. Utilizes state and national-level design manuals in preparation of standard plans. Applies the theoretical background gained in supporting classes, in areas such as traffic analysis, roadway design, roadway drainage, and pavement design. Some review of this material is provided, as well as introduction of several new concepts. Emphasizes teamwork skills and technical communication skills.

name: Advanced Urban Transportation Planning
description: Analytical techniques for estimating future travel demands; and for for planning transportation facilities and locations. Review of transportation technology and future systems.

name: Traffic Engineering
description: Traffic characteristics, studies and analyses, street operations, level of service analysis, congestion and access management, signs and markings, pedestrians, bicycles, parking, roadway lighting.

name: Advanced Transportation Systems Analysis
description: Systems analysis in transportation planning and engineering, including supply, demand, equilibrium, evaluation, and decision analysis.

name: Geometric Design of Transportation Facilities
description: Geometric design criteria and controls of highways and intersections.

name: Pavement Management Systems
description: Evaluation, analysis, design, performance prediction, planning, and maintenance of pavements.

name: Fundamentals of the Transportation Profession
description: Provides a holistic view of the professional practice of transportation including history, organizational structures, legal aspects, finances, human resources, asset management, leadership, marketing and communications, innovation, and technical overview of select topics to prepare students for a career in the field of transportation rapidly undergoing transformation.

name: Freeway Operations and Simulation
description: Uninterrupted traffic flow theory. Highway capacity analysis. Microscopic simulation. Freeway management and control methods.

name: Urban Streets Simulation and Control
description: Principles of simulation modeling and applications. Simulating urban street operations using commercially available packages; traffic signal control and optimization for urban streets; signal control hardware.

name: Traffic Flow Theory
description: Vehicle-roadway-infrastructure interactions, equations of motion, and car-following; microscopic and macroscopic traffic characteristics and traffic stream models; simulation, queueing theory, and shockwave analysis.

name: Highway Safety Analysis
description: Statistics and characteristics of accidents, accident reconstruction, accident causation and reduction.

name: Beginning Turkish 1
description: This course and its sequel, TUR 1131, constitute the introductory sequence in Turkish.

name: Beginning Turkish 2
description: Second semester of the introductory sequence in Turkish.

name: Intermediate Turkish 1
description: Intermediate study of speaking, reading, writing and listening comprehension skills with new vocabulary and grammar.

name: Intermediate Turkish 2
description: Improves speaking, reading, writing and listening skills by building upon language principles introduced in TUR 2220.

name: This Must Be the Place
description: Through a multidisciplinary framework of art, music, history, city planning, urban design, and storytelling, course seeks to address two fundamental questions: 1) How does place work to construct individual and collective identities? and 2) How do collective identities, as expressed through place-based narratives, function to empower and unite communities?

name: Comparative Urbanization
description: Comparative case studies of contemporary cities in the US and a series of foreign countries, both industrialized and developing will be covered. Special consideration is given to energy consumption.

name: Cities of the World
description: Comparative case studies of contemporary cities in the US and a series of foreign countries, both industrialized and developing. Special consideration is given to energy consumption.

name: Preview of Urban and Regional Planning
description: Overview of the comprehensive planning process for those considering a career in urban and regional planning or pursuing studies where some knowledge of the planning process is desirable.

name: 3D Modeling, Visualization, and Simulation
description: Introduces a variety of methods and techniques to interactively model and visualize physical urban environments in two, three, and four dimensions through a hands-on approach using computer software.

name: Survey of Planning Information Systems
description: Introduces concepts and theories associated with Geographic Information Systems (GIS) as related to urban and environmental planning. Requires lectures, class assignments, and homework assignments.

name: Automation for Geospatial Modeling and Analysis
description: Covers methods and techniques for automating geospatial modeling and analysis for planning and built environment by using visual models, computer programming, and custom-built applications and tools that utilize Geographic Information Systems (GIS) technology in the context of planning information systems.

name: Sustainable Urbanism in Europe
description: Explores the diverse urban places that make up modern Europe, its historic development since the pre-industrial city, challenges and accomplishments of urbanization in Europe in recent decades and current accomplishments in achieving sustainable development.

name: Housing and Urban Development
description: Concepts and theories about the economics of the housing market, land development and, home building process, and the growth of cities.

name: Neighborhood Planning
description: An overview of the neighborhood planning process situated within the larger city planning framework.

name: International Perspectives in Urban and Regional Planning
description: Presents contemporary global and critical issues in urban and regional planning by carefully selecting critical topics such as inequality, immigration, and segregation, as well as case studies from around the world. Also encourages the evaluation and development of different strategies and corrective courses of action.

name: Defensible Space and CPTED in Urban Design
description: Explore the history, theory, application, and possibilities associated with crime prevention planning. Investigate theories and strategies in the planner's toolkit and how police, planning, and other agencies interact to implement them. Also focuses on real-world applications and students will visit sites that offer teaching and research opportunities.

name: Exploration and Directed Study: International Field Experience
description: Exploration and directed study.

name: Special Topics
description: Variable topics; lecture, studio, and seminar explore current issues in urban planning

name: Community Service
description: Provides an opportunity to work directly with a community service agency. Public sector agencies, such as a city or county office and nonprofit organizations, qualify as community service agencies. In lieu of meeting in a classroom, students will be placed in a community service agency and will work as volunteers for a minimum of 60 hours during the academic semester.

name: Survey of Urban and Regional Planning
description: An overview of the comprehensive planning process designed for graduates who are considering a career in urban and regional planning or who are pursuing studies, such as urban analytics, where some knowledge of the planning process is desirable.

name: Urban Economy
description: Principles of urban systems, including analytical techniques such as economic base analysis.

name: Community Engagement
description: Provides instruction and hands on experience with community engagement and stakeholder collaboration, especially within an urban and regional planning context and in support of diversity, equity, and inclusion.

name: Planning Administration and Ethics
description: Administration and management of public and private planning offices; ethics of planning profession.

name: Planning Theory and History
description: History of planning and the associated development of theory. Synoptic versus disjointed incrementalism and the political setting for comprehensive planning are emphasized.

name: Land Use Planning Law
description: Introduction to regulatory and nonregulatory techniques of plan implementation. Relationship of law and politics to the planning process. Police power as the basis for regulation. Mandatory planning and status of adopted comprehensive plans.

name: Growth Management Seminar
description: Introducing students with an interest in land use planning to the evolution of growth management planning law in Florida.

name: Planning Research Design
description: Emphasizes research design, and literature research; student presentations at appropriate stages in thesis work.

name: Introduction to Urban Analytics
description: This course introduces Urban Analytics and its applications to real world problems in urban and regional planning, urban studies, and related fields, including urban data sources, processing, visualization, modeling, and analysis methods.

name: Intermediate Urban Analytics
description: This course will provide implementations of Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods into spatial concepts using real world problems in the field. This course will also teach students relevant advanced programming skills to work with spatial datasets.

name: Quantitative Data Analysis for Planners
description: Planning problem formulation, quantitative research skills, and data gathering techniques. Statistical analysis and emphasis on computer applications.

name: Introduction to Planning Information Systems
description: Introduction to concepts, theories, and practice of the use of Geographic Information Systems as applied to urban and regional planning issues.

name: Automation for Geospatial Modeling and Analysis
description: Covers methods and techniques for automating geospatial modeling and analysis for urban planning by using visual models, computer programming, and custom-built applications and tools that utilize Geographic Information Systems (GIS) technology in the context of planning information systems.

name: Urban Spatial Analysis
description: Theoretical and practical knowledge about spatial relationships as applied to urban form and the development and analysis of urban environments using geographic information systems and spatial analysis techniques such as spatial statistical modeling.

name: Intermediate Planning Information Systems
description: Advances technical skills and theoretical/ conceptual skills to allow students to solve intermediate spatial problems using geographic information systems. Students will learn intermediate concepts and skills for data management, editing, analysis, and automation.

name: Web Mapping and Visualization
description: Utilization of web mapping for communication and visualization of geographic data. Includes fundamentals of web GIS, web mapping formats, and spatial architecture, and technical skills for symbolizing data, publishing maps on the web, and creating web mashups.

name: 3D Geospatial Modeling and Visualization
description: Covers methods and techniques for modeling and visualization of physical urban environments in three and four dimensions to help understand, simulate, evaluate, and communicate graphically concepts and ideas about planning and design of built environment. Software used in the course include GIS, 3D modeling, visualization, rendering, parametric modeling.

name: Urban Data Structure Basics
